scope: Post-benchmark provenance audit of already reused MIDI/source/fixtures. No new audio measurement or event correction. All current failed allocator gates remain unchanged.
primary_findings: All 193 same-channel contiguous boundaries in the retained binary SMF have explicit same-track OFF-before-ON byte order. No same-channel raw held duplicate or overlapping gate exists.

Separately rounded onset and gate create 16/16/10/35 one-frame same-channel overlaps in four historical timing maps. This is sample-rounding event distortion, not an inclusive-end +1 or observed hardware overlap.
One genuine simultaneous MIDI62 overlap exists across the two raw channels, plus one cross-channel contiguous MIDI51 boundary; the latter becomes a one-frame overlap only in the robust map.
The parser reproduces all retained note fields exactly; exact rational tempo integration changes no accepted exported onset/gate frame.
The note JSON discards original chord byte order by sorting starts by track and pitch; all four maps reverse 492 within-track ON/ON pair orders. Other same-tick OFF/OFF and OFF/ON orders also differ.
Nominal and robust maps contain no duplicate-ons in either fixed Sine99 support, yet their prior audio gates fail. Overlap counts cannot explain every regression or justify promotion.
Existing video snapshots and exact manual support sampled Mode00 (c.00), not exact receive masks, continuous mode state, actual sender bytes, serial order or arrival times.

protocol.scope: Post-benchmark metadata/source audit; no fresh audio or timing optimization, and no correction to any existing event file. This protocol is fixed before independent raw-SMF decoding/counting in this audit. Previous aggregate duplicate counts and exporter formulas were already known.
tasks: Independently decode every binary SMF event with track ordinal, tick and byte span; integrate tempo exactly using Fraction.
Compare all FIFO-paired notes and original float arithmetic with retained notes JSON.
Reproduce all eight historical/filtered event-file bytes from frozen exporter rules; compare separately rounded gates with directly rounded ends diagnostically only.
Retain every same-pitch adjacent pair and every duplicate-on edge under per-channel and global-MIDI namespaces, including source message order at contiguous boundaries.
Count and distinguish source overlaps, same-tick ordering, parser drift and sample-rounding artifacts for all four fixed maps.
Inspect sampled-mode evidence and explicitly distinguish actual receive-mask/wire unknowns.
Check existing fixed Sine99 supports 176.1..184.2 and 181.55..182.20 without changing windows or rendering audio.

definitions.raw_merge: Canonical analysis order is tick, track index, ordinal. Within-track byte order is established; this canonical intertrack merge is not an observed serial order.
definitions.duplicate: A positive note-on arrives while the namespace key is held; a note-off clears the Boolean key, matching the tested Mode00 input-edge convention. Also report interval overlap independently.
definitions.gap: next_on_tick minus previous_off_tick; negative is interval overlap; zero is contiguous, regardless of same-tick message order.
namespaces: global pitch across accepted MIDI channels
definitions.direct_end: round(48000*(offset+scale*source_end)); diagnostic only, not an adopted fixture.
definitions.exact_time_counterfactual: Repeat historical rounding with Fraction tempo times and exact representations of the fixed float mapping coefficients; isolate parser float drift without changing maps.

restrictions: No new audio extraction/rendering, fitting, sender guesses, event repair, runtime/UI/default/preset/noise changes.
Do not infer all benchmark regressions from overlaps.
No source media or original executable/ROM content is published.

same_tick_order_loss.limits: Intertrack canonical inversions are analysis-order differences, not proven changes to physical serial order. All within-track inversions are against established source byte order; actual sender implementation is unknown.

mode_evidence.previous_visual_scope: 300 preset snapshots plus six late Sine99 snapshots show c.00; existing ledger retains all source-frame hashes.
mode_evidence.this_audit_visual_recheck: Existing late frame003 at181.5seconds visibly reads preset99 and c.00; exact manual printed31 labels c.00 Keyboard Assign and c.99 Sound Source. No new frames extracted.
mode_evidence.actual_receive_mask: Unknown. The displayed c.00 does not show RECEIVE CH. FILTER settings.
mode_evidence.source_file_control_evidence: Raw file has only note-on/off channel messages, plus18meta events. No CC, program change or SysEx can establish the actual MIDI mode, receiver mask or effects.
mode_evidence.conditional_benchmark_policy: Original CPU witness uses explicitly seeded Mode00 and masks1/3. Mapping both raw source channels into one received-key domain is conditional on actual delivery and acceptance of both channels. Source0/1 are raw MIDI channels here, not two independently recorded CV owners.
mode_evidence.continuous_delivery: No continuous receiver/wire log exists. Intertrack same-tick merge remains a deterministic analysis convention, not verified serial order.

limits: Post-benchmark diagnosis, not prospective validation of any replacement fixture.
The retained public MIDI is available and its binary order is known; exact equivalence to the 2017 sender input is not established.
A one-sample numerical overlap can alter Boolean input-edge behavior, but actual serial delivery spans and scheduling are unmeasured.
Directly rounded endpoints remove the studied artificial contiguous overlaps in memory; this is not an adopted fix and does not restore original message order or recover actual gates.
Within-track order is authoritative for the retained file; canonical intertrack order is not authoritative for physical transmission.
No waveform, envelope, phase-reset, release-rate or hardware-fidelity improvement is inferred from metadata alone.
The completed recording comparison remains failed; no allocator/default/native/noise changes follow.
